title: How many sets per week build muscle?
hook: How many sets do you actually need to build muscle?
points: A 2017 meta-analysis by Schoenfeld and colleagues found that people doing ten or more hard sets per muscle each week gained more muscle than people doing fewer than five.
The returns shrink as volume climbs, so more is not always better.
A smart plan: start with a moderate number of sets, and only add more when your progress stalls.
sources: Schoenfeld BJ, Ogborn D, Krieger JW. Dose-response relationship between weekly resistance training volume and increases in muscle mass. J Sports Sci, 2017.

title: Train a muscle once or twice a week?
hook: Do you need to train each muscle twice a week?
points: A 2019 review by Schoenfeld and colleagues concluded that when weekly sets are matched, training frequency does not clearly change muscle growth.
That means the best schedule is the one you can actually stick to.
If you like full body days, great. If you like splits, also great. Just hit your weekly sets.
sources: Schoenfeld BJ, Grgic J, Krieger J. How many times per week should a muscle be trained to maximize muscle hypertrophy? A systematic review and meta-analysis of studies examining the effects of resistance training frequency. J Sports Sci, 2019.

title: How much protein do you really need?
hook: How much protein do you really need to build muscle?
points: A large 2018 meta-analysis by Morton and colleagues found that extra protein helped muscle gain up to about one point six grams per kilogram of body weight per day.
Beyond that, the benefit leveled off for most people.
If you have a kidney condition or any medical issue, check with your doctor before raising your protein.
sources: Morton RW et al. A systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression of the effect of protein supplementation on resistance training-induced gains in muscle mass and strength in healthy adults. Br J Sports Med, 2018.
